body:
The Boston-based firm, majority owned by its partners, exceeded its target by raising close to $27 billion for its 11th flagship fund Advent International GPE XI, according to a statement seen by Bloomberg News. That makes it one of the world’s largest ever buyout funds.

Many private equity firms have been struggling to raise money as their ability to return capital to investors is being stymied. Stubbornly high interest rates are making it harder for them to value portfolio companies and in turn making them reluctant to offload assets to rivals.

Advent raises $30B for buyout and mid-market funds.New flagship fund defies slowdown, securing nearly $27B.Corporate buyers drove strong exits and capital returns.

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Advent has raised $30 billion for its global buyouts strategy and a newer mid-market fund, defying a private equity slowdown with the top pool of capital created in the industry this year.

Those able to exit large assets in this environment are finding favor with investors, who are turning more selective and consolidating their relationships to a handful, rather than a broad array, of private equity companies.

“Despite a challenging year for exits across the market, 2026 has been among the firm’s best years ever, yielding approximately $13 billion in realizations year-to-date,” John Maldonado, a managing partner at Advent, said in an interview. The year was only topped by 2021, the peak of a dealmaking boom.

Rather than relying heavily on sponsor-to-sponsor transactions or initial public offerings, a large portion of exits involved sales to corporate strategic buyers, Maldonado said. This reflects a key theme in private equity this year.

Among these transactions were Advent’s sale of TK Elevator, also backed by Cinven, to Kone Oyj for €29.4 billion ($32.9 billion), as well as a $3.45 billion deal to sell Ultra Maritime to Lockheed Martin Corp.

Advent has also deployed about $10 billion this year so far, Maldonado said. It’s focusing on earnings growth, rather than relying on multiple expansion, and prioritizing take-privates and corporate carve-outs, he added.

The firm, led by a group of managing partners including Maldonado and James Brocklebank, is known for its focus on buyouts. It has repeatedly raised some of the biggest pools of capital in the industry, including its last flagship fund in 2022 at $25 billion.

Other funds of similar size include CVC Capital Partners Plc’s €26 billion vehicle and Clayton, Dubilier & Rice’s $26 billion pool.

Advent also raised more than $3 billion for the new Advent International Mid-Market Private Equity Fund, the statement showed.

Over 50% of commitments for the Advent funds came from public pension funds and sovereign wealth funds, alongside family offices, insurance companies, endowments and foundations, institutional fund managers and high-net-worth individuals, Brocklebank said in the interview. Over 80% came from existing investors, he added.

“Investors strongly backed a focused, pure-play private equity model with a proven track record of returning capital and driving alpha,” he said.

Shweta Jalan, managing partner at Advent, said, “We’re proud to have raised $30 billion across our global fund complex and excited about what it means for India, where Advent has built a strong track record through recent investments including Yatharth Hospitals, Iscon Balaji, Aditya Birla Housing Finance, Svatantra and Apollo 24/7. These funds reinforce our commitment to India and give us even greater capacity to back ambitious entrepreneurs and management teams as they build for the future.”
